title: Submitted the German /de/ set to Bing directly; added scripts/submit-to-bing.mjs
reason: Bing had never crawled a single one of the 11 German URLs nine days after launch, so the German pilot had zero impressions in either engine and the 05 Oct decision gate was measuring crawl scheduling rather than German demand. IndexNow cannot reach Microsoft for this host (their endpoint 403s UserForbiddedToAccessSite), so nothing was ever pushing these URLs to Bing.
author: claude-code
notes: All 11 URLs accepted by Bing Webmaster SubmitUrlBatch on 2026-09-13; quota decremented 100->89 daily, 1800->1789 monthly, confirming acceptance. Verified beforehand via GetUrlInfo that all 11 returned the never-crawled sentinel (year 3939). No page, template, content or tracking change - this is a crawl-queue push only. The new script is owner-run and NOT deployed (scripts/ is .vercelignore d). Re-check with: node scripts/submit-to-bing.mjs --prefix=/de/ --verify. Baseline at submission: Bing 0 impressions on /de/ over 28d, Google 0 over 60d, 1 of 11 indexed by Google, GA4 4 pageviews over 60d.

title: German Expo cluster: keyword-aligned titles/descriptions and in-language cross-links (c-langnote)
reason: The German pilot was technically correct but three of six article titles omitted "Belgrad" - including tickets, whose German query ("expo belgrad tickets") is the strongest German-intent term observed in Bing (9 impressions, position 6.3). "Weltausstellung" and "Serbien" appeared in zero German titles or descriptions, all three DACH pavilion descriptions truncated mid-sentence, and the only English-to-German internal link was a two-letter "DE" header chip carrying no anchor text.
author: claude-code
notes: Titles now all lead with "Expo 2027 Belgrad". what-is-it description now names Weltausstellung (as the contrast it genuinely is - this is a Specialised Expo), guide names Serbien. The three DACH i18n.de.summary fields were restructured into two sentences so metaTrim yields a complete first sentence instead of cutting at "der Kategorie..."; their listing `updated` bumped to 2026-09-13 (drives dateModified + sitemap lastmod). New c-langnote pattern added to globals.css first per the Design Law, then used: an in-content cross-link written in the language it points AT, so all 11 German URLs now have a descriptive anchor-text inbound link from their English twin instead of only the DE chip. German hub H1 keeps the editorial line; only the <title> changed. Sitemap unchanged at 156 URLs; hreflang, canonicals and x-default untouched. Build green.

title: Submitted the 10 remaining never-crawled URLs (2 areas, 8 glossary) to Bing
reason: The same IndexNow gap that left the German set uncrawled had also stranded 10 English URLs Bing had never fetched, including /glossary/bie (Bureau International des Expositions) - Expo vocabulary invisible on the channel that delivers effectively all of the site organic clicks.
author: claude-code
notes: Submitted 2026-09-13 via SubmitUrlBatch; quota decremented 89->79 daily, 1789->1779 monthly (21 URLs submitted in total today with BB-CHG-0003). Identified by a --all --fresh dry-run over the full 156-URL sitemap. Submitted by explicit --prefix rather than a --fresh run: Bing returned transient ErrorCode 2 UnknownError for many URLs during the sweep, which --fresh conservatively skips, so the prefix form is the deterministic one. The script now retries ErrorCode 2 as well as ErrorCode 5 and the runbook records the preference. No page, template, content or tracking change.

title: Reconcile the Expo visitor forecast across all Expo articles (EN + DE) and remove two over-inferences
reason: Our own tracker recorded that the BIE now states more than 6 million visits and that the 6M figure is the more recent, while every visitor-facing Expo article still presented the Participants FAQ 4.1 million model as settled - about 20 statements across 5 English articles and their 5 German twins. The site was contradicting itself on its headline number, and the widely-repeated 44,652/day and 89,304 peak-day figures are derived from the superseded lower model.
author: claude-code
notes: Forecasts are now presented chronologically (2.6-3M earlier statements -> 4.1M Participants FAQ -> organiser arguing 6M -> BIE current 6M+), always labelled projections not counts, with the explicit note that the per-day and peak-day figures come from the 4.1M model and that 6M over 93 days would average nearer 64,500/day. Two over-inferences corrected in the same pass: the tickets claim that most admissions will be digital (1.2M printed tickets include 200k three-day tickets covering multiple admissions, and more can be printed), and the accommodation arithmetic dividing Expo visits by hotel rooms (visits include residents, day-trippers and repeat entries, so they are not overnight demand). The 8,000-events figure is now attributed to the BIE, which publishes it, instead of being called a non-official consolidation. lastUpdated bumped to 2026-09-13 on all ten articles, so dateModified and sitemap lastmod follow. Sitemap unchanged at 156 URLs; no title, URL, template or tracking change. Build green.

title: Trust repair: four factual defects on pavilion profiles and the National Day claim (EN + DE)
reason: An external review pass found that several pavilion profiles contradicted themselves - facts were updated when news landed while hand-written prose and FAQs silently drifted - and one carried a wrong attribution. Publishing new visitor content on top of a self-contradicting record would multiply the correction surface, so this is the precondition for the Expo content plan.
author: claude-code
notes: Slovakia: prose and FAQ said the winning design was not public; facts already named EXPO LINE / Living Playground, announced 9 Jul 2026. Turkiye: prose and FAQ said size was unannounced; facts already gave the 648 m2 plot on parcel A5.1. Austria: prose and one FAQ said the tender was under way while another FAQ named its 4 August 2026 winner - in BOTH languages. Switzerland: the pavilion was described as a walk-through mountain panorama engineered by Werner Sobek AG with Danilo Dangubic Architects and VOGT; verification showed those firms are engaged on the WIDER Expo site (Best Practice Zone timber pavilions, shading structure, landscape), not the Swiss national pavilion - the attribution is removed and replaced with a dated public correction note. Separately, programme.md told readers they cannot pick a date because their country falls on it; Turkiye Ministry of Trade names 19 May 2027 as its planned National Day, so that claim was false - corrected EN + DE, with the Osaka staged-release precedent (131 of 161 dates public about ten months before opening) added as realistic expectation-setting. updated/lastUpdated bumped on all touched records. Sitemap unchanged at 156. No template, URL or tracking change.

title: New page /expo-2027/national-days - the National Day date record, with the date generated from one shared master
reason: A National Day date is the only fact on a pavilion profile that changes which day a visitor travels, and the organiser has not published the country-to-date schedule. Individual countries announce through their own ministries, so this can be built before the organiser publishes. Step two of BELGRADEBEST_EXPO_CONTENT_PLAN.md.
author: claude-code
notes: Deliberately narrow: one question, not a pavilion comparison matrix. Ships with ONE dated entry (Turkiye, 19 May 2027, labelled planned per the Ministry of Trade notice) and one undated announcement (UAE), plus an explicit coverage statement that absence means not-recorded-by-us rather than not-announced. Each dated entry carries what the announcement establishes AND what it does not (times, venue, public access, reservations are all unestablished for Turkiye). Includes the Osaka staged-release precedent as context explicitly labelled not-a-forecast, and the warning that an Expo National Day is not a country domestic national holiday (Osaka counter-examples: Netherlands 21 May vs Kings Day 27 Apr; Sweden 14 May vs National Day 6 Jun). Architecture: src/data/national-days.json is the single master; ListingPage GENERATES the profile National Day row from it and the duplicated fact row was deleted from turkiye.json, so the date cannot drift between the two surfaces - the failure mode that produced BB-CHG-0007. Profiles with a documented date get a tile back to the record; profiles without one do not. Article + Dataset + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. Sitemap 156 -> 157 with lastmod driven by the data master. No German twin yet.

title: Restored 84 article sections lost in the 2026-06-22 content incident; added a build-time integrity gate
reason: Commit e928564 silently dropped whole H2 sections from 17 articles. Repair passes on 2026-07-02 and 2026-08-07 fixed only the ones that ended mid-sentence; the rest ended on a clean full stop and passed every scan, so they were served incomplete for three months. /visit-belgrade/things-to-do-in-belgrade offered 4 of its 10 attractions; best-restaurants lost 55 percent of its body.
author: claude-code
notes: 84 sections (~15,000 words) re-inserted from revision 9645a97 in their original positions; every edit made since June was preserved (sections still present were left untouched). 11 restored sections contain June-2026 prices or opening hours and are UNVERIFIED - flagged for review. New guard src/lib/content-integrity.mjs runs at astro:build:start and fails the build on (a) visible damage and (b) an article shrinking more than 10 percent below a committed baseline; the second check is the one that matters, because punctuation checks cannot detect a section that vanishes leaving a well-formed page. Proven against all three failure modes. Deliberate cuts require committing a re-recorded baseline via scripts/update-content-baseline.mjs.

title: Withdrew the medical-tourism leg entirely (15 articles + hub) - sitemap 157 to 141
reason: Owner research concluded Serbia is not a competitive medical-tourism destination against Hungary, Turkey or Moldova, so the commercial premise does not hold. Independently, the content made consequential treatment-relevant claims the site could not substantiate: a 20-60 percent saving called realistic with no citation, surgical capacity inferred from waiting-list length, ISO listed as an accreditation when ISO does not issue certificates, and an unevidenced ranking of risks.
author: claude-code
notes: Removed from public delivery rather than noindexed - a quarantined page still serves the same guidance to anyone with the link. 15 articles preserved at KB/withdrawn/medical-tourism/ with a README recording why and what a defensible minimum would look like (one logistics page, 4-8 hours, for someone already talking to clinicians). Leg removed from site-schema, header nav, LEGS enum, homepage ethos copy and the About page medical disclaimer; the single cross-link from a retained article was cut; 60 orphaned hero images deleted. Zero dangling /medical-tourism links remain in the build. Fully reversible: files, flags and README are all in-repo.

title: Removed FAQPage markup that described invisible content; dropped the unevidenced Source-checked claim
reason: ArticleLayout emitted FAQPage JSON-LD for 422 questions (~27,000 words across 64 English and 6 German articles) that the layout never rendered, so the markup described content no reader could see. The two copies had already drifted - the airport article FAQ gave a rail date its own body contradicted. Google retired FAQ rich results on 2026-05-07, so the markup also bought nothing.
author: claude-code
notes: faqSchema call removed from ArticleLayout; homepage FAQ schema now gated on the same visible flag as its section, which had the same defect. Frontmatter faqs retained as editorial source material to fold into bodies during page edits, not as a separate maintained copy. Separately: every article carried Updated <date> - Source-checked by the BelgradeBest editorial process, attached automatically to any dated page with no evidence of a source review and no visible sources; reduced to the date. The About page claim that every page is manually reviewed and nothing goes live unread was replaced with an accurate account including the June content loss and the new guard.

title: Structural pass: main landmark + skip link, TOC de-paginated, heroes off practical pages, decision-point links, homepage re-ordered around tasks
reason: Completing the content-audit workplan (items 5-9). The measured problem was that the short answer arrived first but the section that does the work sat behind a decorative hero and a table of contents that hid its own later entries; the homepage led with an event eight months out for an audience that is mostly not searching for it.
author: claude-code
notes: (1) BaseLayout now renders one <main id=main> for every public page plus a localised skip link; articles previously had NO main landmark at all (header, 4 navs, article, footer). index.astro lost its own duplicate. Footer navs get aria-labelledby pointing at their visible headings. New .c-skiplink pattern added to globals.css first, per the Design Law. (2) ArticleToc no longer paginates into horizontal slides of 10 behind arrows - it hid sections 11+ from the list whose job is to reveal them; 11 articles were affected and eating-and-drinking-in-belgrade had 8 of its 18 sections invisible. All items now render in one two-column list; the inline slider script is gone. (3) Practical legs (plan-your-trip) no longer render the decorative hero: first body section moved from byte 6155 to 1758. The hero is still generated and still used as the OG/social card via meta.image. Leisure legs keep theirs. (4) Contextual links added at three decision boundaries rather than only in the bottom gallery: dinars beside the cash-only A1 fare, connectivity beside the ride-hail data requirement, airport transfer costs beside the airport-exchange warning. (5) Homepage re-ordered identity -> Start here (7 task routes to real articles) -> browse all -> compact Expo feature -> credibility; the FAQ section was cut as a duplicate of the task block, which also removes its JSON-LD. (6) FAQ frontmatter deleted from the two reviewed articles - all 15 questions were already covered in their bodies, and the removal takes the contradictory airport rail date with it. Sitemap unchanged at 141.

title: Homepage simplified to 270 words; per-article feedback voting rejected in favour of a contact invitation; integrity gate bypasses closed
reason: Two owner questions - is the homepage good from a modern UI perspective, and should every article carry a thumbs up/down with results hidden. External review answered: shorten rather than redesign, and kill the voting system because 114 real sessions per 60 days cannot produce a decidable sample. Review also found a defect shipped earlier the same day and an over-claim in the About page.
author: claude-code
notes: DEFECT FIXED: the two quick-answer cards added earlier that day used a `body` field while GoodToKnow.astro renders `text`, so both shipped as a label with no answer - in a section promising a straight answer to each. Homepage then: cut to six quick answers (Where to stay has a nav entry and a category card directly below), removed the duplicate Start here eyebrow, deleted two filler intros, hid the standalone Expo feature (it was still a full-width 21:9 hero, so moving it down had changed order not weight), and reduced the credibility block to one sentence plus an About link. 515 -> 270 words. Kept the narrow-intro/full-width-grid convention (deliberate --readw reading measure, not a defect) and both card treatments. FEEDBACK VOTING REJECTED: at ~114 sessions/60d a 5 percent response rate is about 6 self-selected answers site-wide, which cannot support rankings or before/after claims, and the listing-request storage pattern (GitHub commit per write, rebuild trigger, no rate limiting or dedup) is far too heavy for an anonymous thumb. Shipped instead: a plain contact invitation on three arrival-decision articles, no endpoint, no scores, results never public. Reopen condition recorded: a named article, a specific unresolved question, an owner who will read responses, and plausible exposure for 50 responses in 60 days. INTEGRITY GATE: a missing baseline made the check silently vacuous, an emptied body was skipped, and an article deleted from disk was invisible - all three now fail the build. The About page claim that the gate refuses to publish a page that has lost content was false and is narrowed.
